solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Jest how sins have upset a member of a Christian group (8,7)

annotation.definition: a member of a Christian group

indicatorNotes.upset: something upset is knocked over, so its letters land in a new order

annotation.surface: Someone is offended by a joke about sinning, as a devout believer might be.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole four-word phrase supplies the fodder, including the innocent-looking 'have', which reads as part of the sentence rather than raw material.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: the denomination founded in 1870s America calls itself Christian, and each adherent takes the group's name in the singular.

entries.clue: Jill’s companion on vessel gets big pay-out (7)

blocks.note: Jack and Jill of the nursery rhyme
in a down clue, the first piece sits on top of the next

annotation.surface: A nursery-rhyme boy boards a ship and lands a fortune.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but it is the humbler pot.
annotation.definitionFit: The top prize in a lottery or on a fruit machine, the biggest sum that can be paid out.

entries.clue: Mother only holds bird (5)

indicatorNotes.holds: the phrase holds the answer inside its letters, the way a hand holds a coin

annotation.surface: A mother is the only one keeping hold of a bird.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mother' tempts you toward MA or MUM; the letters simply run across the gap between the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: A long-legged wading bird, a definition by broad category.

entries.clue: Vehicle by university within top city (9)

indicatorNotes.within: 'within' puts the university inside the lid: U sits in the middle of COVER

blocks.note: a top or lid is a cover

annotation.surface: A van parked beside a university in a leading city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Top city' reads as the definition, but 'top' is the COVER that holds U; only 'city' defines.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the largest city of British Columbia, on Canada's Pacific coast.

entries.clue: Harassed husband turned up, very withdrawn (7)

indicatorNotes.withdrawn: something withdrawn is taken away, so V for very is pulled out

blocks.note: to turn up is to arrive
remove V (very) from ARRIVED, leaving ARRIED

annotation.surface: A hassled husband arrives home, painfully shy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' in a down clue looks like a reversal instruction; here it simply means arrived.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words describe someone pestered and worn down by constant demands.

entries.clue: Rings people who do cleaning (7)

blocks.note: the flat metal rings fitted under a nut or inside a tap
those who scrub dishes, cars or clothes

annotation.surface: A phone call, or a summons, to the cleaning staff.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rings' reads as a verb, calling the cleaners; it is the noun, the flat metal rings.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: a small flat ring used with a bolt, and someone who washes things.

entries.clue: Initially, tigers advancing tear up mammal (5)

indicatorNotes.Initially: 'initially' means at the start, so each of the next two words gives its first letter
indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, going up means reading the word from bottom to top

annotation.surface: Tigers close in and maul some other animal.
annotation.walkthrough: The tigers set up a hunting scene; the mammal is the tapir, a pig-like browser of the forest.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by broad category: a hoofed, long-snouted beast of the tropical forests.

entries.clue: Save awfully nice moose (9)

indicatorNotes.awfully: done awfully means done badly, so the letters come out in a mess

annotation.surface: A plea to rescue a very sweet moose.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Save' reads as rescue; it is the thrifty sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the money sense: to cut spending and put cash by.

entries.clue: One day, briefly, I consumed stuff (7)

indicatorNotes.briefly: said briefly, a day's name shrinks to its three-letter abbreviation

blocks.note: SAT is the short form of Saturday

annotation.surface: Someone recalls a day when they ate a lot of food.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' looks like a noun at the end of the sentence; it is the verb, to fill up with food.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym as verbs: to fill someone with food until they want no more.

entries.clue: Official investigator in nook holding nothing (7)

indicatorNotes.holding: a word that is holding something has it inside, so CORNER wraps round O

annotation.surface: An investigator searches a corner and finds nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: The nothing is placed after the first three letters of the nook.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: the public officer who holds inquests into sudden or suspicious deaths.

entries.clue: Drink fortified wine – keep up! (7)

annotation.surface: A drinking companion urges you to keep pace with the port.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Keep up!' sounds like an order to match someone's drinking; it means hold up, bear the weight of.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym in the literal sense of bearing weight, holding something so it does not fall.

entries.clue: Performance of Greek god with cat? I’m ecstatic, originally (9)

indicatorNotes.originally: 'originally' means at the origin, the start, so 'ecstatic' gives its first letter

blocks.note: Pan, the Greek god of the wild
a tom is a male cat

annotation.surface: A theatregoer is thrilled by a show starring a Greek god and a cat.
annotation.walkthrough: A pantomime is the British Christmas stage show with slapstick, songs and audience participation.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the Christmas family stage show is one kind of theatrical show.

entries.clue: Wine starts to rot in old jars, actually (5)

indicatorNotes.starts to: the starts of the following words are their first letters

blocks.note: first letters of Rot In Old Jars Actually

annotation.surface: A wine is beginning to spoil in its ancient jars.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is a Spanish red named after the region in northern Spain where it is made.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a Spanish red from the upper Ebro valley.

entries.clue: Damaged hive grabbed by Edward – it’s stolen (7)

indicatorNotes.Damaged: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so HIVE's letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.grabbed by: to be grabbed by someone is to end up in their clutches, so TED closes round the letters

annotation.surface: Edward makes off with a broken beehive, and it is theft.
annotation.walkthrough: The rearranged hive sits between the T and the ED of Ted.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are past participles of verbs meaning to take what is not yours.

entries.clue: Person from cold country arranged fire and candle, leaving France (9)

indicatorNotes.arranged: letters that are arranged are put in a deliberate new order
indicatorNotes.leaving: F, the code for France, is leaving: it walks out of FIRE

blocks.note: F is the international code for France

annotation.surface: A northerner lays out a fire and candles and quits France.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'and' merely joins the two pieces of fodder; only IRE and CANDLE are rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful description: the North Atlantic island nation is chilly despite its green south, and its people take its name.

entries.clue: Saint and a king eat fish (7)

annotation.surface: A saint and a monarch sit down to a fish supper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Eat fish' reads as the meal; 'eat' supplies DINE and only 'fish' defines.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a small oily member of the herring family, often tinned.

entries.clue: Check, then declare it’s put back as before (9)

blocks.note: to rein in is to check

annotation.surface: Someone verifies something, announces it, and restores it to its place.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Check' reads as verify; it is the restraining sense, as with a horse's rein.
annotation.definitionFit: A paraphrase: to restore someone or something to a former position or condition.

entries.clue: Chaps saving cold caviar for tennis star (7)

indicatorNotes.saving: to save something is to keep it safe, here tucked inside MEN

blocks.note: C = cold, as on a tap

annotation.surface: Men keep chilled caviar aside for a tennis champion.
annotation.walkthrough: The cold sits just after the M of the chaps.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: John McEnroe, the fiery American who won seven Grand Slam singles titles.

entries.clue: Oddly, main small group of actors given wrong parts (7)

indicatorNotes.Oddly: 'oddly' means in the odd places, so 'main' gives its first and third letters

blocks.note: M(a)I(n): the first and third letters
a cast is the group of actors in a show

annotation.surface: The leading members of a small troupe have been badly cast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' belongs to 'main' alone; the rest is read straight.
annotation.definitionFit: A paraphrase in theatre terms: actors assigned roles that do not suit them.

entries.clue: Bring the setter around pub, then leave: it’s prohibition! (7)

indicatorNotes.around: to bring someone around is to turn them to face the other way, so ME becomes EM

blocks.note: the setter = ME, brought round to EM

annotation.surface: The setter is taken to the pub and then told to go, as if drink were banned.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Around pub' suggests ME placed around BAR; instead 'around' turns ME itself, and BAR follows.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym: an official order forbidding trade or movement, a ban.

entries.clue: Give vile, yet revealing, hostile stare (4,3)

indicatorNotes.revealing: the words are revealing, uncovering what lies within their letters

annotation.surface: Someone shoots a nasty, telling glare.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface describes a glare while the letters hide one.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to give someone the malevolent look is to glare at them with ill will.

entries.clue: Put under a spell, with inclination to lose head (7)

indicatorNotes.to lose head: a word that loses its head loses its first letter

blocks.note: a penchant is an inclination, a liking

annotation.surface: Someone bewitched is tempted to lose their head.
annotation.walkthrough: A liking, stripped of its first letter, becomes the spell.
annotation.definitionFit: A literal sense: to cast a spell on, as a sorcerer does, before the weaker sense of delight.

entries.clue: He’s in fabulous, revolutionary, unfinished old city (7)

indicatorNotes.in: HE'S is in, placed inside the other letters
indicatorNotes.revolutionary: a revolution is a full turn, so the letters turn round and read backwards
indicatorNotes.unfinished: a word left unfinished has its ending cut off

annotation.surface: Someone is in a marvellous, rebellious, half-built ancient city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' reads as rebellious; it is the turning sense. The city was a Greek port on the coast of modern Turkey.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a ruined Greek city of Asia Minor, home of the Temple of Artemis.

entries.clue: Show mercy to Prince Harry? (5)

blocks.note: to let someone off harm or punishment
the younger royal son, backup to the heir; the question mark flags an example

annotation.surface: A plea for leniency toward Prince Harry.
annotation.walkthrough: Harry, second son of King Charles, is known as 'the spare' to his brother the heir, and titled his 2023 memoir Spare.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: to let off unharmed, and the nickname for the second-born royal kept in reserve.

entries.clue: Run more (5)

blocks.note: in cricket, a run not scored off the bat, such as a wide or bye

annotation.surface: An instruction to jog further.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket, byes, wides and no-balls are runs credited to the team rather than the batsman.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: a cricket run not off the bat, and an adjective meaning additional.

entries.clue: Puts bet on whip to obtain key sign (9)

blocks.note: to back a horse is to bet on it

annotation.surface: A gambler bets on the whip hand to get a vital signal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Key sign' suggests music; the key is on a keyboard.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful description: the leftward-leaning stroke printed on a computer keyboard key.

entries.clue: A model uprising for storyteller (5)

indicatorNotes.uprising: in a down clue, a word rising up is read from bottom to top

annotation.surface: A fashion model leads a rebellion in a tale.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Model uprising' reads as a revolt; 'uprising' is the reversal instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the ancient Greek credited with the fables of the tortoise and the hare.

entries.clue: Inspector in raid, out partying (7)

indicatorNotes.partying: letters out partying are running wild, so they end up in a new order

annotation.surface: A police inspector joins a raid while off-duty colleagues are out partying.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Inspector' suggests police, which the raid supports; it is the financial inspector.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym in the financial sense: the person who examines a company's books.

entries.clue: Assembles in American services (7)

annotation.surface: Someone gathers people together in American military services.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Services' suggests the armed forces; these are church services.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym: both mean gathers together into a collection or heap.

entries.clue: Jane’s wild fellow, a real swinger? (6,2,3,4)

annotation.definition: Jane’s wild fellow, a real swinger?

blocks.note: reads as a girlfriend's unruly boyfriend; the jungle man raised in the wild, whose partner is Jane
reads as a party animal; really someone who swings through trees on vines

annotation.surface: Jane's boyfriend is an untamed party animal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swinger' suggests a partygoer; Tarzan literally swings through the trees on vines, and he was raised by apes.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes Edgar Rice Burroughs's jungle hero, Jane's mate, who travels by vine.
